name: Kadai Paneer

ingredients.name: Kashmiri dried red chilli (sukhi lal mirch)

equipment: Small tawa or pan for dry-roasting spices
Mortar and pestle (khal-batta) for grinding the kadai masala
Mixer-grinder (small jar) to purée the tomato
Small bowl for soaking paneer, and a plate to hold the fried capsicum and onion
Measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp ≈ 5 ml)

steps.title: Measure the whole spices
steps.text: Put 1 tsp coriander seeds, 2 Kashmiri dried red chillies (stems removed, broken in half, most seeds shaken out), ¼ tsp cumin seeds and 3 black peppercorns in a small bowl.
steps.tip: shaking out the chilli seeds keeps the heat mild; the colour stays.
steps.visualCue: four small heaps of whole spices
steps.videoShot: chillies broken in half and seeds shaken out

steps.title: Dry-roast the spices
steps.text: Heat the small pan on low. Add the spices with no oil and stir constantly.
steps.tip: if anything smokes or turns black, start again; burnt masala tastes bitter.
steps.visualCue: coriander turns a shade darker and smells warm and citrusy; chillies turn crisp but stay red, not black
steps.videoShot: spices being stirred in a dry pan

steps.title: Cool the spices
steps.text: Tip them onto a plate and spread them out.
steps.visualCue: cool to the touch, chillies snap easily
steps.videoShot: spices tipped onto a steel plate

steps.title: Grind the kadai masala
steps.text: Pound the cooled spices in a mortar and pestle (or grind in the small mixer jar) to a coarse powder.
steps.tip: a slightly coarse grind is traditional and gives little bursts of flavour.
steps.visualCue: rusty-red, coarse powder with small coriander husk flakes; strong toasty smell
steps.cameraCheck: the ground masala in a small bowl (about 1½ tsp)
steps.videoShot: pestle crushing spices

steps.title: Chop onion for the masala
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: small, even pieces
steps.videoShot: knife chopping onion finely

steps.title: Cut onion petals
steps.text: Cut 30 g (⅓ small) onion into 2 cm squares and separate the layers.
steps.visualCue: loose, flat onion squares
steps.videoShot: fingers separating onion layers

steps.title: Cut capsicum
steps.text: Remove the seeds and white pith from 60 g (½ medium) capsicum and cut it into 2 cm squares.
steps.visualCue: even green squares about the size of the paneer cubes
steps.videoShot: capsicum diced on the board

steps.title: Purée tomato
steps.text: Roughly chop 100 g (1 medium) tomato and blend it in the small mixer jar to a smooth purée.
steps.visualCue: smooth, bright-red purée
steps.videoShot: tomato purée poured into a bowl

steps.title: Prep ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Peel and finely chop 5 g ginger and 2 garlic cloves. Slit 1 green chilli lengthwise.
steps.visualCue: three small heaps
steps.cameraCheck: ginger, garlic and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: garlic cloves being chopped

steps.title: Cube and soak paneer
steps.text: Cut 100 g paneer into 2 cm cubes and cover with warm (not boiling) water.
steps.visualCue: even cubes submerged in water
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of paneer cubes in water
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes slid into warm water

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on high heat and add 2 tsp (10 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers and flows freely when you tilt the pan
steps.videoShot: oil swirling in the kadai

steps.title: Stir-fry capsicum and onion petals
steps.text: Add the capsicum and onion petals and toss on high heat.
steps.tip: take them out early; they cook again at the end.
steps.visualCue: a few light brown spots on the edges; capsicum is bright green and still crunchy
steps.videoShot: capsicum and onion tossed in the hot kadai

steps.title: Set them aside
steps.text: Lift the capsicum and onion petals onto a plate, leaving the oil in the kadai.
steps.visualCue: oil left behind in the pan
steps.cameraCheck: the plate of capsicum and onion
steps.videoShot: vegetables lifted out with the spatula

steps.title: Sauté chopped onion
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium. Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: soft and light golden at the edges
steps.videoShot: onion sizzling as it's stirred

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the chopped ginger, garlic and slit green chilli and stir.
steps.visualCue: raw garlic smell is gone
steps.videoShot: ginger and garlic stirred into golden onion

steps.title: Add tomato purée
steps.text: Pour in the tomato purée, add the pinch of turmeric and half the salt, and stir.
steps.visualCue: bright red, loose masala
steps.videoShot: red purée poured into the pan

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Cook on medium, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.tip: it splutters; partly cover the pan. If it sticks, add 1 tbsp water, not more oil.
steps.visualCue: masala thickens, turns a deeper red, and small drops of oil appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, tilted to show oil at the edge
steps.videoShot: thick masala bubbling with oil at the rim

steps.title: Add most of the kadai masala
steps.text: Lower the heat. Add about 1¼ tsp of the fresh kadai masala (keep about ¼ tsp for the end) and stir.
steps.visualCue: masala smells toasty and spicy, not burnt
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, and the small amount of masala kept aside
steps.videoShot: rust-red powder sprinkled and stirred in

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 80 ml (⅓ cup) water and the rest of the salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: thick gravy that coats the spatula
steps.cameraCheck: the spatula lifted out of the gravy
steps.videoShot: gravy dripping slowly off the spatula

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Simmer on low, partly covered.
steps.visualCue: gentle bubbles; gravy slightly thicker
steps.videoShot: gravy bubbling lazily

steps.title: Add paneer
steps.text: Drain the paneer and add the cubes. Fold gently.
steps.visualCue: every cube coated in red gravy
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes folded into the gravy

steps.title: Add capsicum and onion back
steps.text: Add the stir-fried capsicum and onion petals and fold.
steps.visualCue: green capsicum and onion squares spread through the curry
steps.videoShot: green capsicum tipped back in

steps.title: Simmer briefly
steps.text: Simmer on low.
steps.tip: longer than 3 minutes makes the paneer chewy and the capsicum soggy.
steps.visualCue: paneer warmed through; capsicum still has a bite
steps.videoShot: slow bubbles around paneer and capsicum

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: aroma becomes noticeably "restaurant-like"
steps.videoShot: kasuri methi crushed between palms

steps.title: Add the rest of the kadai masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in the reserved ¼ tsp kadai masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed, fresh spice smell
steps.videoShot: last pinch of masala sprinkled over

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off. Stir in 2 tsp (10 ml) fresh cream.
steps.tip: adding cream with the heat off stops it splitting.
steps.visualCue: gravy turns a slightly lighter, glossy orange-red
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled through the red gravy

steps.title: Garnish and plate
steps.text: Taste for salt, sprinkle 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves and spoon into a bowl.
steps.visualCue: semi-dry red curry with white paneer and green capsicum
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the finished bowl

reasons: Paneer gives ~18 g protein and plenty of calcium, and capsicum, tomato and onion add vitamin C and some fibre. Nothing is deep-fried, there's no added sugar, and the flavour comes from freshly roasted whole spices rather than fat. Fat is still fairly high (~34 g, much of it saturated from paneer and cream). Restaurant versions often fry the paneer, use butter and more cream, add cashew paste, and are saltier.

researchRating.basis: a staple of North Indian restaurant menus and one of the most-cooked paneer curries at home, with very high recipe ratings. Common complaints are rubbery paneer, soggy capsicum, and a "flat" taste when store-bought powders replace fresh kadai masala; a meal-kit review summary also notes some found it bland.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 2 days (est.). The capsicum softens and the paneer firms up after a day. Freezer: not recommended with paneer and capsicum (both turn watery and spongy); the gravy alone freezes for up to 1 month (est.). Reheating: gently on the stove on low with 1–2 tbsp water, just until hot, or 1–1½ minutes in the microwave covered, stirring once. Don't boil.
leftoverRemix: Kadai paneer frankie. Cook the leftover curry down until almost dry, roughly mash a few paneer cubes, then spread it on a warm roti with a little green chutney, raw onion rings and a pinch of chaat masala, and roll it up tightly. Toast the roll on a tawa for 30 seconds a side.
burnOff: about 6.6 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 9.3 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).
